description: Pass rules of the fresh evaluation that closes D34 step 6 (docs/BENCHMARK.md 6.14). Two things are judged with new SfM runs of commons-ten-v1. (1) Settings.facing_away_warns_other_refs, the fourth switch (d): a photo whose compass heading points away from the building and is not tagged true north is kept with a warning instead of being rejected. It changes which photos are accepted, so no replay can show it. (2) The georegistration defaults chosen by offline replay in eval/criteria/d34-v1.json ((a) gps_span_model_side, (b) compass_other = ignored; (c) yaw_arbitration stays off): a replay cannot see which candidate a job picks among its mapping attempts nor the retries, which under (b) now read true-north headings only. This file was written before any fresh D34 run existed (2026-11-12, from 5fa4619): the dev rule and the held-out rules are frozen here; the dev outcome and the config nominated for the held-out run are added below (dev_outcome) before the held-out run, and no rule is changed after a number is seen. The rules are judged by compare --criteria d34b-v1 with the documented noise handling (noise factor 1, the noise blocks of the two results and of every result of the test set at this metric schema in eval/results/commons-ten-v1/); the checks read the result files, compare's JSON and the run directories, and are judged outside compare.

A.what: The D31 fresh runs (d31-dev.json, d31-test.json: 09f7621, two repeats, the request caps below) as rescored at metric schema 8 in 716de16 without restylizing. compare refuses d31-<split>.json itself (metric schema 7); d30-a-<split>.json holds the same runs' metrics and their own two-repeat noise block and is what compare takes its noise from. Georegistration as recorded: every D34 switch at its old behaviour, facing_away rejecting whatever the tag.

A_same_georegistration.what: Report only: the same D31 SfM output replayed under (a) + (b) ignored (on the held-out split the three-switch arm, in which (c) overruled nothing, so it equals (a) + (b)). B against this A differs by (d), by a new draw of the SfM, and by what a replay cannot show.

B.commons-ten-v1 dev: run --testset commons-ten-v1 --config d34-heading-warn --name d34-dev --repeat 2 --time-cap 3600 --max-requests brandenburg-gate=104 frauenkirche-dresden=31 --buildings florence-baptistery aachen-cathedral brandenburg-gate leaning-tower-pisa frauenkirche-dresden --reference-cache <scratch>/d34/g1b-georeg-fresh/refs/commons-ten-v1 --resume
B.commons-ten-v1 test: run --testset commons-ten-v1 --config <held_out.nominated> --name d34-test --repeat 2 --time-cap 3600 --buildings sagrada-familia hungarian-parliament lincoln-memorial india-gate sydney-opera-house --reference-cache <scratch>/d34/g1b-georeg-fresh/refs/commons-ten-v1 --resume
B.what: Fresh runs (COLMAP), stylize on, one building at a time, from a clean committed tree; the request caps and repeats of the D31 runs. The reference cache is a copy of the one the D31 runs and the D34 replays read (India Gate reference version 2).

decisions: D34 (owner, 2026-11-10): implement the code review's recommendations. The lead's brief for this step: measure with fresh SfM; decide (d) from the dev split; freeze config and criteria; run the held-out split once; (d) stays off if it fails; a georegistration default that fails on the fresh run although it passed on replay is reported plainly and set off; nothing is tuned after a held-out number.

Why B is compared with d30-a-<split>.json and not with a d-off run of today's code: the brief asks for the committed D31 baseline and its noise floor, and one fresh run per split. The difference B - A therefore holds (a), (b), (d) and a new draw of the SfM together. Two things separate them: the paired replay of the fresh run itself under the old georegistration (fresh_pair, below: the same SfM output and the same accepted photos, so it shows (a) + (b) alone, without noise), and the per-photo account of what the newly accepted photos did (newly_accepted_photos).

The stated thresholds are those compare gives today; they can only rise with the fresh runs' own run-to-run spread (compare takes the largest recorded spread). Two repeats understate noise (docs/BENCHMARK.md 8); a guard that fails is still a FAIL here.
wrong_face_cameras_shown and gt_gross_shown are judged on every building as well as on the split (as in d31-v1): (d) adds photos to single buildings, and a split total can hide one building's harm.
No cost rule: the same work took about 1.5 times the CPU on this machine a day apart (docs/BENCHMARK.md 6.12), more than any effect of 12 to 30 more photos; cpu_time_s is reported.

predicted_acceptance.how: From the photo rows of the recorded D31 runs (summary.json of every repeat; both repeats agree): a photo rejected for facing_away alone whose heading is not tagged true north is accepted with (d) on. Validation does not depend on SfM, so a funnel that differs is a program error, with one exception that is then named: a newly accepted photo can make a later near-identical upload a duplicate.

thresholds_today.how: compare's threshold of a split aggregate is max(the metric's smallest change, its relative floor x A, noise factor 1 x the largest spread of that aggregate recorded in a noise source); of one building, the same with that building's largest recorded spread. Noise sources today: d30-a-dev, d30-a-test. B's own noise block is a source too, and d34-dev's for the held-out pair.

georeg_baseline.how: benchmark.py georeg's errors over the distinct checked models of A (published, georegistered, at least 3 unflagged cameras with a verified, oriented reference pose); between_its_two_repeats: the same errors over each repeat's checked models, r1 against r2.

dev_rule.written: 2026-11-12, before the fresh dev run; committed with the config, from which that run is made.
dev_rule.d_is_nominated_when: no guard rule below and no guard check below FAILS on the dev pair (a rule or check that is INSUFFICIENT on dev is named and does not block)
dev_rule.if_a_guard_fails: (d) is not nominated: the held-out run is made with config d_off (the defaults), as the fresh confirmation of (a) + (b) alone. One exception, decided on dev numbers only: a second fresh dev run with config d_off may be made, and (d) is nominated if the d_on run passes the same guards with that run as A (the failure was then not (d)'s).
dev_rule.noise_on_dev: A not_worse guard on a summed count that fails by compare's threshold on dev is not held against (d) when the change is within the sum of the dev buildings' recorded spreads of that count (the bound compare itself uses for a split aggregate, compare_results' noise_bound). The recorded spread of the dev aggregate can be 0 while two buildings each vary by 1 between repeats (facades_published in d30-a-dev: Aachen and Pisa). Such a guard is named with both numbers. No such allowance is made on the held-out split.
dev_rule.reported_not_decisive_on_dev: fresh_pair on the dev run (the paired replay under the old georegistration) and A_same_georegistration: (a) and (b) were chosen on these five buildings already

held_out.nominated: config d_on when dev_rule nominates (d), else d_off; written into dev_outcome before the run
run_once: the B command of commons-ten-v1 test above (the only COLMAP run of the held-out split)
rescore --testset commons-ten-v1 --from <d34-test.json> --name d34-fresh-own-test --restylize --replay default --reference-cache <the same cache>
rescore --testset commons-ten-v1 --from <d34-test.json> --name d34-fresh-off-test --restylize --replay eval/configs/d34-regeo/off.json --reference-cache <the same cache>
held_out.verdict_d: PASS when every guard rule and every guard check of this file passes on the pair A = d30-a-test, B = d34-test and the precondition holds; FAIL when one fails; INSUFFICIENT when none fails and one lacks data. Judged only when (d) was nominated.
held_out.verdict_georegistration: d34-v1 applied to the fresh run as that file defines its verdict, on the pair of replays of d34-test (check fresh_pair): PASS when its rules and checks all pass; FAIL when one fails; INSUFFICIENT when none fails and one lacks data.
defaults: verdict_georegistration PASS: gps_span_model_side and compass_other = ignored stay the defaults. FAIL or INSUFFICIENT: both go back to the old behaviour (they qualified on dev only together), RECON_OUTPUT_VERSION is raised, and (d) stays off whatever its verdict (it was measured with them on).

verdict_d PASS and verdict_georegistration PASS: facing_away_warns_other_refs becomes the default (on), RECON_OUTPUT_VERSION is raised. verdict_d FAIL or INSUFFICIENT, or (d) not nominated: it stays off.

verdict_d FAIL with verdict_georegistration PASS: the failing guards are listed with the models and poses behind them and whether a newly accepted photo is among their cameras; what a replay cannot show of (a) + (b) (candidate choice, retries) is then not separated from (d) and is reported as open.
yaw_arbitration is not under test and stays off.
Every held-out result is kept and reported whatever it shows; nothing is tuned afterwards.

checks.require: every building and repeat of B ran to the end: status ok, not truncated by the time cap, the same number of upload requests as A; compare lists no building with different inputs; B was made from a clean committed tree with the frozen config
checks.how: B's result file (buildings[].repeats[].status, details.truncated, details.requests against A's, provenance.git, config.sha256) and compare's buildings_inputs_differ. A building that fails this is named; the pair is then INSUFFICIENT, not FAIL.
checks.why: A run cut short uploaded fewer photos: its counts are not comparable with A's.

checks.require: photos_accepted of the split rises (compare: delta > 0 and significant; the recorded noise of this count is 0), and every building's funnel in every repeat equals predicted_acceptance: accepted = accepted_predicted, the warning heading_away_unverified on newly_accepted photos, facing_away = facing_away_predicted, every other rejection reason as in A
checks.how: each repeat's summary.json funnel (uploaded, accepted, rejected_by_reason, warnings). A funnel that differs from the prediction is listed photo by photo; it fails the check unless the split still rises and each difference is a duplicate of a newly accepted photo. Only with config d_on.
checks.why: What (d) is for: dev 460 -> 472 accepted photos per run, held-out 399 -> 429.

checks.require: photo_pose_uncertainty_coverage (the share of shown poses with a reference pose that lie within their own stated 2-sigma range, pooled over the split) is not lower beyond noise: compare's row of the split is not (delta < 0 and significant)
checks.how: compare --json: splits[<split>].photo_pose_uncertainty_coverage. The metric has no direction in compare, so a rule cannot judge it; the same threshold applies (thresholds_today).
checks.why: The ranges shown with a pose must stay honest.

checks.require: over the distinct checked models of the split (benchmark.py georeg): RMS |ln scale| and yaw RMS of B not above A's by more than max(5 % of A's value, the difference between A's two repeats, the difference between B's two repeats); the share of checked models with the scale off by more than 35 %, and with the yaw off by more than 15 deg, not worse beyond sampling noise (95 % Newcombe interval of B - A, benchmark.rate_worse)
checks.how: georeg_errors of each result's calibration rows (pooled over the repeats as georeg does, and per repeat by the rows' run); numbers of A in georeg_baseline. No checked model in B: INSUFFICIENT.
checks.why: The compare rules read medians of building medians; the review's findings are about the models far off, which an RMS and the off-counts see.

checks.require: the photos accepted with the warning heading_away_unverified, every repeat counted: none is an unflagged camera of a published model whose yaw is 30 deg or more off the reference (wrong_face); and, when at least 10 of their shown SfM poses have a verified reference pose, the wrong share among those is not worse than the wrong share of the other photos' shown SfM poses beyond sampling noise (benchmark.rate_worse). Fewer than 10: that part is reported, not judged
checks.how: each repeat's summary.json (photos[]: warnings, the shown pose's source and model, its verdict against the reference) and the stored models' cameras (flags). Listed per building: accepted, registered in any model, registered in a published model, flagged there and with which flag, shown by SfM / by position only, right / wrong / no reference, in a wrong-face model. Only with config d_on.
checks.why: A photo that really looks away may register on something else or not at all; the check says what the kept photos did.

erratum.what: Two fields of the frozen predicted_acceptance were wrong for a photo rejected for facing_away AND another reason whose heading is not tagged true north: with (d) on it stays rejected for the other reason, but loses the facing_away code and carries the warning heading_away_unverified. So the facing_away count is the photos tagged true north (not facing_away_predicted), and the warning is on every facing_away photo not tagged true north (not on newly_accepted alone). The accepted counts were predicted right. Found on the dev run (Brandenburg Gate: facing_away 4 not 5, warned 4 not 3; one photo, also not_subject) and corrected here before any held-out number exists. It corrects a predicted count and loosens no harm guard; check accepted_photos_rise is read with these numbers, and its verdict by the frozen numbers is recorded next to it.
erratum.recomputed_from: the photo rows of the recorded D31 runs (summary.json of every repeat; both repeats agree)

newly_accepted_photos_account.what: A report, not a verdict. The photos the d_on dev run accepted with the warning heading_away_unverified (12 per run; both repeats agree on everything but the SfM poses' errors), per building. Looking at the building: the angle between the reference viewing direction and the direction from the reference position to the landmark centre is within the 60 deg validation's facing check allows. Per-photo rows are not committed.
newly_accepted_photos_account.reading: Of the 12 photos per run, 7 are unflagged cameras of published models and are shown by SfM (the 3 of them with a reference pose are right in both repeats); 5 are shown by position only (Pisa 1, Frauenkirche 4), none of those in a published model. All 6 with a verified reference pose look at the building (0.7 to 32.9 deg off the direction to its centre). They had been rejected because the heading reading is wrong (3 photos: 80, 114 and 137 deg from the reference viewing direction) or because the EXIF position is wrong (3 photos: 24, 48 and 102 m from the reference position; their headings are within 6, 14 and 33 deg). Looked at by eye, the 4 Frauenkirche photos shown by position only are: a statue with another building behind it, the church not in the picture (registered in no model: with (d) on such a photo is accepted and shown as a position marker); the square with the church in the right third of the frame (EXIF position 48 m off); a neighbouring palace with the church at the edge of the frame (102 m off); the church's choir from below. The second of them registered in three unpublished models, among them the N facade model (7 of 9 registered), where it is flagged far_from_gps (115 m) and the gate then failed that model (2 of 7 cameras flagged). The N facade model of the D31 run and of the d_off fresh run (6 of 8 registered, published) has a reference scale of 0.31 to 0.32 and 4 wrong shown poses. The cameras behind the gt_gross_shown failures are none of these 12 photos: at the Brandenburg Gate the E facade's displayed model is another job's (request 99, 53 of 61 registered, reference scale 1.09 and 0.99 in the two repeats) than without (d) (request 101, 52 of 59, 1.01 to 1.05), and 2 and 1 of its other cameras are 21 to 23 m off the reference; at the Frauenkirche the NE facade's displayed model is the job of request 6 (6 of 8 registered, not georegistered) instead of request 11 (8 of 8), with one camera 21 m off.

what_a_replay_cannot_show.what: A report. The d_off fresh run against the recorded D31 run (A of the frozen pair) differs by (a) + (b) and by a new draw of the SfM only: the two accepted the same photos, so every job has the same key (request, kind, sector, number of photos). same_sfm_model: the job kept a model with the same number of registered images and of points.

what_a_replay_cannot_show.reading: Photos accepted are the same as in the D31 run on every building (460). Of 238 jobs with the same key (both repeats), 219 registered the same number of photos as in the D31 run and 139 kept a model with the same number of points; 19 registered another number (Pisa 16, Aachen 1, Brandenburg Gate 1, Frauenkirche 1). The split aggregate: published models 68.5 -> 66, facades with a model 20 -> 19, shown poses 317 -> 310, right 142.5 -> 146.5, wrong 78.5 -> 68.5, gt_gross_shown 1.5 -> 1. The replay of this fresh run under the old georegistration (fresh_pair_reported.of_the_d_off_run) separates the two causes. The new draw of the SfM, judged by the old rules: published 68.5 -> 66.5 (Aachen -0.5: the SE facade job of request 29 registered 5 of 24 photos in both fresh repeats, 10 in one D31 repeat; Pisa -1.5: 12 and 10 in the D31 repeats, 10 and 9 here; in r1 the full model and the NE facade model of request 33 are not published, in r2 the W facade job of request 22 registered 4 of 25 photos; no fresh repeat publishes a full model, one of the two D31 repeats did), right 142.5 -> 140, wrong 78.5 -> 75. (a) + (b) on that same fresh SfM output: published 66.5 -> 66 (Pisa +1, Frauenkirche -1.5: SW facade models fail the gate's compass check, 3 and 4 per repeat, as the D31 replay had shown), right 140 -> 146.5, wrong 75 -> 68.5, the same +6.5 / -6.5 the replay of the D31 run gave. What a replay cannot show, from nine single-job reruns (18 job runs; every model of every attempt judged under both parameter sets): in 14 of 18 runs both sets rank the same model first, among them every rerun job of Aachen, the Brandenburg Gate and Pisa; where a fresh job registered fewer photos than the D31 job (Aachen request 29, Pisa request 22 W, Pisa request 33 full) the rerun shows a draw of the SfM, not the ranking: the Pisa full job yields an 87-image model with 19 flagged cameras and a 73- or 75-image model from the cut re-map with 5 or 8, 68 unflagged against 68 or 67: the cut model wins the tie on its compass error, the 87-image model wins by one camera, under both sets alike. The two sets differ at the Frauenkirche only. (1) Equal-size models tie when a job has magnetic readings only (NE facade jobs: 6 magnetic, no true-north reading): the defaults keep the first attempt, the old rules the one with the lowest compass error; the displayed NE model has the same reference scale as in the D31 run (0.58 and 0.62 against 0.58 and 0.62). (2) The full-building job of request 21 (58 photos, 24 magnetic and 1 true-north reading): under the old rules 8 cameras disagree with GPS and compass, the twin-facade cut re-map runs and its model wins (43 images in the rerun, 7 in the D31 run); under the defaults the magnetic readings do not count, no cut re-map runs and the 51-image model is kept, 27 of its cameras far from their GPS. Neither is published. So in these reruns the candidate choice and the retries under the defaults made no published or displayed dev model worse; they do lose the evidence magnetic readings gave of a twin-facade mix. Not rerun: 15 of the 19 jobs whose registered count differs (14 at Pisa, 1 at the Brandenburg Gate). Requests 44 E and 69 SE of the Brandenburg Gate and the NE facade of the Frauenkirche, which the d_on run had raised: request 44 (13 of 25 registered in d_on r1, 22 in every other repeat of every run) gives a 22-image model in every attempt of the rerun under both sets; request 69 is the same 5-image model under both sets, georegistered under the old rules and not under (a) (4 of 5 GPS fixes over 8.4 m); the NE facade's prior_only model of the d_on run is the job of request 6 (6 of 8 registered), not georegistered in any of 6 attempts under the defaults and in 5 of 6 under the old rules.

nomination.rule: dev_rule as committed: (d) is nominated when no guard fails on the frozen pair (after noise_on_dev), or, through the exception run, when the d_on run passes the same guards with the d_off run as A; otherwise it is not nominated and the held-out run is made with config d_off.

dev_outcome.reading: On dev the fresh run with (d) on accepted exactly the 12 more photos predicted (460 -> 472 per run) and failed three guard rules of compare against the recorded D31 run. Two of them (models_published 68.5 -> 66, facades_published 20 -> 18) are within the sum of the dev buildings' recorded spreads and are not held against (d) (dev_rule.noise_on_dev). gt_gross_shown 1.5 -> 3.5 is held against it: the aggregate's change exceeds that sum, and the Brandenburg Gate (1 -> 2.5) and the Frauenkirche (0 -> 1) are significantly worse by themselves. The exception run (the defaults, fresh, the same commit) has gt_gross_shown 1 at the Brandenburg Gate and 0 at the Frauenkirche in both repeats, as the D31 run has; with it as A the run with (d) on fails the same guard (1 -> 3.5, the same two buildings). So (d) is not nominated: the held-out run is made with config d_off, as the fresh confirmation of (a) + (b) alone, and facing_away_warns_other_refs stays off whatever that run shows. The per-photo account (newly_accepted_photos_account) is a finding, not a verdict: the photos (d) lets in mostly do look at the building, and none of them is one of the cameras behind the failing guard; the guard fails because a facade with more photos gets another model, in which other cameras cross the 20 m line. Two repeats of the same uploads do not measure that kind of change, so turning (d) on needs paired runs of its own (d_on against d_off, fresh, the same code) with more repeats. (a) + (b) on fresh SfM output are reported in what_a_replay_cannot_show and fresh_pair_reported; they are judged on the held-out split by held_out.verdict_georegistration, not here.

held_out_outcome.reading: The one held-out run was made with the nominated config d_off (the defaults) from the commit that recorded dev_outcome; it ran the code of the dev runs, every building and repeat to the end, and accepted the same 399 photos as the recorded D31 run. verdict_d is not judged: (d) was not nominated, so facing_away_warns_other_refs stays off. verdict_georegistration is PASS: d34-v1 on the run's own replays (old georegistration against the run's parameters, the same SfM output) is met on every part. The replay under the run's own parameters equals the plain rescore (145 of 145 models replayed, none moved). Helps: yaw RMS 7.69 -> 6.84 deg (-11.1 %), right poses 61.5 -> 64.5 with wrong 35.5 -> 32.5. No harm: published models 25.5 -> 26.5, shown poses 186 -> 186, beyond their own 2 sigma 12.5 -> 11.5, no wrong-face model or camera, the four coverages not lower, scale-off models 6 -> 6, yaw-off models 2 -> 1. Stylization not worse on 40 values; d34-v1's two rules pass. So gps_span_model_side and compass_other = ignored stay the defaults, yaw_arbitration stays off, and RECON_OUTPUT_VERSION stays 4: no default changes. As in the replay of the D31 run, nearly all of the gain is Sagrada Familia (yaw median 7.13 -> 4.76 deg, right 38.5 -> 41.5, wrong 7.5 -> 4.5, one more published model); the Hungarian Parliament, the Lincoln Memorial and India Gate are unchanged by (a) + (b) apart from one yaw value, and Sydney Opera House publishes no model in either. Reported, not a verdict: against the recorded D31 run the fresh run reads better or the same on every guard row of this file but one, geo_yaw_error_median_deg (2.99 -> 4.09 deg, threshold 0.5), which is the new SfM result at the Hungarian Parliament and is larger still under the old georegistration (5.20). Nothing was tuned after the run.

narrows.why: The proof given for them is the replay of the fresh run under the old georegistration. A replay makes the georegistration, the camera checks and the gate again on the SfM models the jobs kept. It cannot show which candidate a job would have kept among its mapping attempts, nor its retries (dev_outcome.what_a_replay_cannot_show), and the fresh run was made to expose exactly that. So the replay excludes the georegistration arithmetic of (a) + (b), not their job-time path; why this building's value rose had not been looked into when the two sentences were written.
narrows.reads_now: Shown: the rise is not an effect of the georegistration arithmetic of (a) + (b) (the replay); (b) cannot have acted at job time in any W facade job of the Hungarian Parliament, the jobs whose models make this building's value (none of their photos has a heading (b) treats differently); (a) left the ranking count and the flagged cameras of every kept model of the building as they are under the old rules (30 of 30 stored models). Not shown: whether (a) would have ranked the candidates that lost differently. They are not kept, and no job was run again: the frozen file allows one COLMAP run of the held-out photos. The row stays a reading that fails.

Per run: every mapping attempt as [attempt, registered photos, flagged cameras] from the harness log, the attempt kept, what the summary says of the kept model, whether it counts in the building's value, and its |yaw error| against the reference in degrees. what_it_shows: Request 32 (21 photos): the first attempt is kept in all four runs, with 13 photos registered and 2 cameras flagged each time; its |yaw error| is 5.3 and 0.94 in the D31 run, 4.65 and 5.82 in the fresh run. Request 28 (18 photos): published only in the D31 run's first repeat, the one run where an attempt came out with 1 flagged camera (the kept attempt has 3 in the other three); that model is 0.4 deg off, one of the two models of that repeat's median (the other is request 32's 5.3).

Request 41 (38 photos), the model on display: the D31 run kept the first attempt in one repeat (31 registered) and the second in the other (29); the fresh run the second (29) and the first (32). The D31 run's 31-photo model is 7.62 deg off but was not georegistered (15 of 31 GPS fixes consistent, fewer than half), so it does not count in the D31 value; the three others count with 2.5, 10.11 and 5.74 deg.
Request 25 (15 photos): published only in the fresh run's second repeat (an attempt with 2 flagged cameras; 3 or 4 everywhere else), 6.97 deg off.

b_cannot_act_in_the_w_jobs.what: compass_other acts only on a heading that is not tagged true north. The eight W facade jobs (6 to 38 photos; the one with 6 found no initial pair) hold nested photo sets, the same uploads in all four building runs. Of the 38 photos of the last one, 35 have no compass heading and 3 are tagged true north; none is magnetic or untagged. So in these jobs every candidate, kept or lost, its ranking, the retry and the QA compass check are the same under "trusted" and "ignored".

a_on_the_kept_models.what: Every stored model of the building in the fresh run (15 per repeat, published or not), its kept SfM model judged as a job judges a candidate, under the defaults and under params.AS_BEFORE.

the_38_photo_job.what: The only W job above Params.small_set_images (30): a second attempt is made only when the first is suspicious (more than 5 % of its cameras flagged, or a compass error above 20 deg), and it is a re-map with the pairs cut when two or more cameras are off both their GPS and their compass. The first attempt had 6 to 8 of 31 or 32 cameras flagged in all four runs; all four took a plain second attempt, none a re-map. Unflagged cameras of the two attempts, the kept one first:
the_38_photo_job.what_would_change_it: In the fresh run the kept candidate leads by 3 unflagged cameras in both repeats. Judged under the old rules the kept ones count the same (26 and 26). The ones that lost (31 registered with 8 flagged, 29 with 6) would need 3 fewer flagged cameras under the old rules to draw level; only (a) could do that here. Their flags under the old rules are not known.

job_time.not_separated: Candidate choice at the W jobs under the old rules against the defaults was not separated by a rerun. What stands against an effect of (a): no flag moved on any of the 30 kept models. What would settle it: each W job run again under both parameter sets with every candidate kept, which is COLMAP on held-out photos and was not done.

dev_reruns.what: Support from the dev split only: the nine single-job reruns recorded in dev_outcome.what_a_replay_cannot_show.single_job_reruns (each job run with COLMAP under both parameter sets, every candidate of every attempt judged under both). Counted here: the candidates on which (b) cannot act (no reading counts differently between the sets), and what (a) alone changed on them. The compass error is the ranking's third part, a tie-break.

lost_twin_pair_signal.what: What (b) does change at this building, the same thing dev showed at the Frauenkirche: the two full jobs whose registered cameras include magnetic readings. Unpublished under either rule set (13 to 23 of 47 or 58 photos registered; a full model needs 70 %).

request_31_full_47_photos.reads: In the D31 run the first attempt of repeat 1 had cameras off both their GPS and compass (compass error 76.74): the job re-mapped with their pairs cut and kept that model; repeat 2's kept model failed the gate for twins and compass among other reasons.
